02 / Experience

Where I've
worked.

Four internships in two years. The running lesson has been that the algorithm is almost never the hard part. It's everything standing around it.

Summer 2026

Capital One

Software Engineering Intern

I built a Slack assistant for operations teams. It streams answers token by token, stops and asks a person before doing anything it shouldn't decide alone, and runs on ECS Fargate underneath. By August it was fielding questions for ten different teams.

  • 2,500+ people across 10 teams ended up using it
  • 100+ queries a day, response time cut roughly in half
  • Streaming SSE pipeline with human-in-the-loop interrupts
  • Dockerized on AWS ECS Fargate, conversation state in DynamoDB
2025 – 2026

Empower AI

Software Engineering Intern

Fraud, waste, and abuse detection on federal healthcare data. I built the pipelines that got thirty million records into usable shape, and the evaluation setup that told us whether a model was genuinely better or had just gotten lucky on one split.

  • 30M+ Medicare and Medicaid records through the pipeline
  • 97% accuracy and 98% recall on anomaly detection
  • Isolation Forest, LOF, and one-class SVM, packaged for audit
  • Reproducible evaluation so results survived review
Summer 2025

Ackuity

Software Engineering Intern

A Chrome extension that catches sensitive information on its way into ChatGPT and other AI tools, and redacts it before it ever leaves the browser. It has to happen as you type, which is a much stricter constraint than it sounds.

  • 40+ kinds of PII and credentials caught in real time
  • Working across 3 major LLM platforms
  • Fine-tuned DistilBERT on 40,000 synthetic examples, exported to ONNX
  • Two-tier confidence thresholds to keep false positives survivable
Spring 2025

Kihara Bioinformatics Lab

Machine Learning Research Intern

My first research job. I wrote a custom reward function and a PPO pipeline to push AlphaFold2 toward better predictions on beta-amyloid structures, then presented what came out of it to the lab. Learning to defend a result is its own skill.

  • 100+ protein structures evaluated
  • 5% lift on the target structural metric
  • PPO training pipeline in Python and PyTorch
  • PyRosetta and PyMol for preprocessing and simulation
